tasks.old_behavior: git-gui browser|blame accepted arguments with a heuristic parser: (1) path-before-rev ordering was supported via worktree file-existence check, (2) rev validation only for hex-looking strings, (3) no path existence validation in the target rev, (4) loosely structured argument iteration with ambiguous is_path flag logic.
tasks.new_behavior: git-gui browser|blame uses strict positional argument parsing: (1) path must be the last argument (required), (2) rev is optional and validated with git rev-parse --verify, (3) path is validated with git ls-tree to verify it exists in the target rev, (4) --line=<num> strictly enforced as first arg for blame only, (5) -- separator supported for explicit rev/path boundary.
tasks.compatibility_reason: The undocumented path-before-rev feature (e.g., "git gui blame lib/blame.tcl gitgui-0.6.0") was removed. Scripts relying on this argument ordering will break. Argument validation is now stricter - revs must be valid git refs and paths must exist in the target revision. Users passing invalid or out-of-order arguments will now get clear error messages/usage instead of potentially confusing displays.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test git gui blame/browser with various argument orderings, invalid revs, non-existent paths, --line combinations, and -- separator usage to verify strict parsing and error messages.
